basis.governing_question: Where can Iberia Foods identify savings of 8% of the cost base without cutting service levels?

sub_questions.question: What does the cost base look like today across the twelve workstreams?
Which service levels must the savings protect, and how are they measured today?
Where are the savings opportunities, and how large is each?
Which opportunities hold the service levels, and do they add up to 8% of the cost base?
What savings program should the CFO and COO sign off, and in what sequence?

drivers.evidence: They want it run as twelve workstreams

work.unit: Interview round with one stakeholder group
Function savings opportunities sized against service levels
Savings program built and tested against the 8% target

phase_work.why: Interviews run three at a time, sizing four at a time; twelve functions put it above the archetype's 3 to 6 weeks.

sizing.levers: Interview and size the largest cost functions in depth and cover the rest from data; running more functions at once would also shorten it.

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Baseline costs and service levels across twelve functions, then design the savings program toward the 8% target.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the sized savings program as the final result?

architect_notes: One Diagnostic phase, the closest fit, with design inside it: twelve workstreams across two phases would need 24 rows, over the 12 allowed.
The stated 12 weeks all go to the one phase; the work estimate runs 11 to 20 weeks.
Assumed driver: twelve stakeholder groups to interview, one per function, which sets 4 to 8 weeks of the estimate; confirm with the client.
No Implementation phase: the brief is an assessment only, so the performance improvement archetype stops after its Diagnostic.
